entities.name: Yiran Qaghan
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Yollıg Khagan, also known as Yiran Qaghan, was the fifth ruler of the Second Turkic Khaganate, reigning from approximately 726 to 739 CE. He was a key figure in the Turkic expansion into Central Asia and Eastern Europe.


Yiran Qaghan played a crucial role in shaping the geopolitics of the region, particularly in the relations between the Turkic Khaganate and the Tang Dynasty of China.


His reign marked the beginning of a period of significant cultural and economic exchange between the Turkic peoples and the Chinese, which had lasting impacts on the development of the region.


Despite his relatively short reign, Yollıg Khagan left a lasting legacy in the annals of Turkic history, cementing his place as one of the most influential figures of the Second Turkic Khaganate.


As a testament to his enduring impact, Yiran Qaghan's name remains etched in the annals of history, a testament to the power and resilience of the Turkic people.
